evidence: Plaut. Trin. 339: dē mendīcō male merētur quī eī dat quod edit aut bibat
Cic. Fin. 5.84: mendīcus esse beātus nēmō potest (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Properly an adjective, needy, beggarly; as a noun, a beggar (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Plaut. Capt. 323: mendīcantem vīvere, to live by begging
Suet. Aug. 91.2: stipem … ēmendīcābat ā populō, he begged alms from the people
terms.comment: Also deponent, mendīcor (Plaut.); to beg something from someone, ēmendīcāre.

phrases.latin: animadvertī pauperem mendīcum, jam, crēdō, saturum, jocantem atque laetantem
phrases.english: I noticed a poor beggar, already full, I suppose, joking and cheerful

phrases.latin: aequō mendīcus atque ille opulentissimus cēnsētur cēnsū ad Acheruntem mortuos
phrases.english: among the dead by Acheron the beggar and the richest man are rated at the same worth

sources: Lewis & Short: mendicus · Lewis & Short: mendico
